key_insight: A room-temperature methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into bromide perovskites, enabling a universal, solvent-free synthesis route for multiple metals.
engineering_relevance: This strategy could simplify and scale manufacturing of optoelectronic perovskite films, with strong compatibility for ambient processing and roll-to-roll fabrication.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt as the reactive brominating medium.
React elemental metal films directly at room temperature to form MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4.
Tune melt composition to control reactivity and suppress unwanted oxidation, especially for Sn.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful phase conversion for Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu, with in situ XRD observing transient intermediates in two cases and high-quality MASnBr3 formation under ambient conditions.
watch_item: Reaction outcomes depend on metal redox behavior and polybromide composition, so overoxidation and phase-control may remain challenging for some metals or scaling conditions.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
